clue.text: Incorporate the sailor's sphere

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is the usual sailor; with the possessive it gives ABS
an orb is a sphere or globe

explanation.surface: An instruction to fold a seaman's globe into something.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'S of 'sailor's' is kept as a letter here: AB'S plus ORB.
explanation.definitionFit: To absorb something is to take it in and make it part of a larger whole.

clue.text: Support a cause and marry

explanation.surface: Someone backing a campaign and getting wed.
explanation.definitionFit: To espouse means both to adopt and champion a belief, and, in older use, to take as a spouse.

clue.text: Spend a long time asleep camouflaged in the brae

indicators.note: camouflaged means disguised, so the letters of these words are rearranged out of recognition

explanation.surface: An animal sleeps for months, hidden on a Scottish hillside.
explanation.walkthrough: A brae is a Scottish hillside, which suits the sleeping animal of the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Animals that hibernate pass the winter in a long dormant sleep.

clue.text: Throws away the bandages

explanation.surface: Someone discards dressings they no longer need.
explanation.definitionFit: To sling is to toss carelessly, and slings are supporting bandages for an injured arm.

clue.text: Multitudes of fishes come to the shallow waters

explanation.surface: Huge numbers of fish swim into the shallows.
explanation.definitionFit: Shoals are large groups of fish, and the word also means sandbanks or shallow places at sea.

clue.text: Temporarily dispense with a rugby player

explanation.surface: A coach drops one of his rugby team for a while.
explanation.definitionFit: To stand off workers is to lay them off for a time, and the stand-off half is a rugby back position.

clue.text: Neat curve of lake

parts.note: neat is an old word for cattle, so one beast is an ox
a bow is a curved shape, as in a bent stick

explanation.surface: A tidy bend in the shoreline of a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Neat' poses as an adjective meaning tidy; it is the old noun for cattle.
explanation.definitionFit: An ox-bow lake forms when a river meander is cut off and left as a curved pool.

clue.text: Not for heavy drinkers presumably

parts.note: read as a drink that is the opposite of heavy, a pale weak beer, rather than one for people who drink a lot

explanation.surface: A remark that something is unsuitable for people who drink a great deal.
explanation.walkthrough: In Scotland 'heavy' is a type of beer, so the drink that is not heavy is its lighter cousin.
explanation.definitionFit: This pale, lower-strength beer is the reverse of a heavy brew.

clue.text: William, note, has a way in prison

indicators.note: in shows the next pair of pieces placed inside the first pair

parts.note: Bill is the short form of William
ST, street, is a common abbreviation for a way or road
E is one of the musical notes A to G

explanation.surface: A man called William and a musical note find a route into jail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' is a link; 'in' puts A and ST inside BILL plus E, giving B-AST-ILL-E.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bastille was the Paris fortress used as a state prison, stormed in 1789.

clue.text: Sack in French station contains rubbish

indicators.note: contains shows the French word for station holding the word for sack inside it

parts.note: gare is French for a railway station
a sack is a bag

explanation.surface: A sack left at a French railway station holds refuse.
explanation.definitionFit: Garbage is waste or trash thrown away.

clue.text: Wizard place, one with clean bracing air

parts.note: Oz is the land of the Wizard of Oz

explanation.surface: A magical land and one breath of fresh air.
explanation.definitionFit: Fresh seaside air is popularly called this gas, thought of as invigorating.

clue.text: Begin in earnest as one in the basement may have to do

definitions.text: as one in the basement may have to do

explanation.surface: Someone getting started properly, compared to a worker who has to go downstairs.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is literal: someone whose firm is in the basement must go downstairs to reach it.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means to start serious work, and literally to descend to one's place of trade.

clue.text: Letter carried by a messenger

indicators.note: carried by means the letters sit inside the word that follows, as cargo in a vehicle

explanation.surface: A courier delivers a letter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Letter' looks like the post the messenger carries; it is the name of a letter of the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: The spelt-out name of the nineteenth letter of the alphabet.

clue.text: See 11
Household pest I am unfortunately taken in by

indicators.note: taken in by means the scrambled letters go inside the word for pest

parts.note: a fly is an insect pest

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things gone wrong, so the letters of these words are disordered

explanation.surface: A home suffers an insect pest, and the speaker is fooled by it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfortunately' turns I AM into AMI, which goes inside FLY.
explanation.definitionFit: A household is the people living together under one roof, that is, the relatives at home.

clue.text: Speed does not matter whatever may happen

explanation.surface: Someone says the pace is unimportant, come what may.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally the phrase means at whatever speed; idiomatically it means in any case.

clue.text: One cannot sleep through it

parts.note: read not as a noise too loud to sleep through but as the condition that itself keeps one awake

explanation.surface: Something so disruptive that nobody could sleep through it.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a racket that wakes you; the answer is the sleeplessness itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Chronic inability to fall or stay asleep is a medical sleep disorder.

clue.text: Draw a piece clothing

explanation.surface: A drawn match and an item of dress.
explanation.walkthrough: The print seems to have lost 'of' from 'a piece of clothing'.
explanation.definitionFit: A drawn game ends in a tie, and a tie is a neckwear garment.

clue.text: An example of how golfers might differ

definitions.text: An example of how golfers might differ

parts.words: An example of how golfers might differ
parts.note: read as two words: golfers differ in the way they stand to address the ball

explanation.surface: An illustration of the ways golf players vary.
explanation.walkthrough: Split it as IN STANCE: golfers differ in how they stand, while the whole word means an example.
explanation.definitionFit: An instance is a single case or example of something.

clue.text: A short distance behind

parts.note: FT, feet or foot, is the abbreviation of a short length

explanation.surface: Something lies a little way back.
explanation.definitionFit: Aft is the nautical term for towards the stern, the back of a ship.

clue.text: Invisible passage for translation has not been prepared

definitions.text: passage for translation has not been prepared

explanation.surface: A test text for translation that the student never saw coming.
explanation.walkthrough: In British schools an 'unseen' is a passage given to translate without preparation.
explanation.definitionFit: Unseen means not visible, and an unseen is a foreign passage translated at sight.

clue.text: Take advantage of employment

explanation.surface: Someone exploits a job.
explanation.definitionFit: To use someone is to exploit them, and use as a noun means application or employment of a thing.

clue.text: I will take attendant out to plunder

indicators.note: out says the attendant sits on the outside, round the contraction

parts.note: a page is a young attendant
I'll is the contraction of I will

explanation.surface: Someone takes a servant along on a looting raid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take' is a link; 'out' puts PAGE on the outside of I'LL, giving P-ILL-AGE.
explanation.definitionFit: To pillage is to loot or ransack, especially in war.

clue.text: Does no one sit down at a meeting of it?

definitions.text: Does no one sit down at a meeting of it?

parts.words: Does no one sit down at a meeting of it?
parts.note: read the name of a permanent council literally, as a body whose members are always upright

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about a meeting where nobody takes a seat.
explanation.walkthrough: The first word of the phrase means permanent, but read literally it means upright, hence nobody sitting.
explanation.definitionFit: A permanent council kept in being rather than formed for one task, here pictured as never seated.

clue.text: Sent in from this game

indicators.note: from here means the game's letters are made from the letters of the preceding words

explanation.surface: A ball sent in from the court during a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' tells you to build the game out of the letters of SENT IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Tennis is a racket sport played over a net.

clue.text: Get Ray somehow to move round

indicators.note: somehow means by some unspecified means, so the letters are rearranged in some way

explanation.surface: Persuade a man called Ray to turn around.
explanation.definitionFit: To gyrate is to spin or whirl in a circle.

clue.text: See 23
Island mother left with little gratitude

parts.note: ma is a familiar word for mother
ta is a short British way of saying thank you

explanation.surface: A mother is left on an island with barely a thank-you.
explanation.definitionFit: Malta is an island nation in the Mediterranean.

clue.text: Liner, Queen Elizabeth II

explanation.surface: The name of an ocean liner, Queen Elizabeth II.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as the famous ship; 'liner' is a drawer of lines, and the queen is a sovereign.
explanation.definitionFit: A straight-edge draws lines, and a monarch such as Elizabeth II governs a realm.

clue.text: Well, sort of, Heather has a suspicion

parts.note: an inkwell is a sort of well, so the kind of well gives ink
ling is a common heather

explanation.surface: Someone named Heather admits she has a vague hunch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heather' reads as a woman's name; it is the plant, ling. 'has' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An inkling is a slight hint or vague notion.

clue.text: Stay put as cannot stand being drunk

parts.note: someone unable to stand must sit
tight is slang for drunk

explanation.surface: Someone stays where they are because they are too drunk to get up.
explanation.definitionFit: To remain where one is and wait without acting.

clue.text: One is in position in a large building

indicators.note: is in means the letter for one sits inside the word for position

parts.note: a place is a position
a is the indefinite article, one

explanation.surface: Somebody stands in their spot within a big building.
explanation.definitionFit: A palace is a grand residence, a stately and imposing building.
